From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Certify-to-close checklist and eval test plan (Ava Health MAP)

Hi Priyanka —

Thanks again for the time today. As discussed, I pulled together a concise 'certify-to-close' checklist that maps the MAP milestones to acceptance tests and owners. The objective is to make sign-off deterministic: if the acceptance tests in the attached plan pass and the evidence items are uploaded to the shared folder, we consider the eval complete and move to contract execution + production onboarding cadence.

High-level asks in this draft:
- Target close window: customer sign-off by 2026-12-10 (flexible by mutual agreement).
- Core success criteria: functional accuracy, 90th-pctl tail latency <= 350ms for 99% of production-like traffic, embedding similarity recall >= 92% on the curated 2k sample, and no PII leakage in 10k red-team prompts.
- Exit gates: smoke pass on core flows, compliance evidence (SOC2 audit snapshot), and a Canary run with 1% of traffic for 48 hours showing stable CPU/GPU and KV cache hit-rate >= 60%.
- Acceptance tests: attached acceptance_test_plan.md enumerates test cases, owners, data sets, and pass/fail thresholds.

Attachments: [attachment: MAP_certify_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)], [attachment: acceptance_test_plan.md (text/markdown)].

Can you review the criteria and call out any must-haves from your side (particularly around compliance and data residency)? If this looks good we can lock owners and dates and send the MAP for signature (I can route via DocuSign).

Next step I propose: 30-minute sign-off sync the week of 11/22 to finalize owners and schedule the Canary.

Thanks —
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Redwood Inference — Developer-first LLM inference platform

Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Certify-to-close checklist and eval test plan (Ava Health MAP)

Hannah —

Thanks for the clear draft. A few immediate notes from our side:

1) Compliance evidence: we need a current SOC 2 snapshot and an outline of the KMS/HSM setup for any private deployment. Please attach the SOC2 attestation or an auditor letter if available.
2) Latency: 350ms 90th is fine for most paths, but for the single-turn clinician query path we need 95th pctl <= 300ms under our staging load (we can provide the staging load profile).
3) Edge cases: can you add an explicit brownout / rate-limiting test and a data-residency verification test (we must confirm logs and KV cache are stored in us-east region for this eval).
4) Signatures: we prefer DocuSign routing directly to our legal/ops after MAP finalization.

I'll loop in James (ops) and our compliance mailbox so they can review acceptance_test_plan.md. Attaching our internal compliance checklist for reference.

Attachments: [attachment: ava_compliance_checklist.pdf (application/pdf)].

Best —
Priyanka Rao

Hannah —

We reviewed the proposed updates internally. We can accept the additional clinician-query 95th threshold and the brownout test as part of the acceptance rubric. A few clarifying points before we finalize:

- Brownout scenario: please define an automated traffic throttle and a fallback messaging behavior for model timeouts (we need the exact failure mode the application will surface).
- Data residency evidence: we will want a signed attestation from Redwood that logs and KV cache snapshots are stored in us-east-1 for the eval.
- Canary: 1% traffic for 48h is acceptable; we also want resource metrics (GPU util, memory, KV hit-rate) sampled at 1m granularity during the run.

I've attached our compliance checklist; James will provide the staging load CSV later this week. Once you update acceptance_test_plan.md with the brownout steps and the attestation entry, please send the MAP via DocuSign to me and cc our legal (legal@avahealth.com).

Subject: Finalized acceptance rubric (next steps & owners)

Team / Priyanka —

Thanks for the quick turn. Summary of agreed items (finalizing now so Soojin can route DocuSign):

1) Success criteria (must pass all to sign off):
   - Functional correctness: embedding recall >= 92% on curated 2k sample (owner: Ben C.).
   - Latency: general 90th <= 350ms; Clinician Query 95th <= 300ms under staging profile (owner: Ben C.).
   - Security/compliance: SOC2 snapshot + KMS diagram posted to Drive (owner: Marissa C.).
   - No PII leakage above threshold on red-team prompts (owner: Marissa C.).
   - Canary: 1% live traffic for 48h with GPU Utilization, memory, and KV hit-rate sampling at 1m granularity (owner: Hannah S.).

2) Exit gates (all required):
   - Smoke tests pass end-to-end (basic flows).
   - Compliance evidence uploaded and attested (SOC2 + data-residency attestation).
   - Canary metrics show stability for 48h (no critical alerts).

3) New acceptance tests added per request:
   - Brownout / rate-limiting test (simulate 3rd-party timeout + degrade to cached response; pass if user-facing latency bounded and error rate <= 0.5%).
   - Data residency verification (console export + signed attestation).

4) Timeline & next steps:
   - 11/19: Marissa to upload SOC2 snapshot + KMS diagram to Drive.
   - 11/20: Ben to update acceptance_test_plan.md with clinician-query test, brownout steps, and measurement hooks.
   - 11/22–11/26: Run Canary prep; schedule 30-min sign-off sync on 11/23 (09:00 PT).
   - 11/29–12/01: Canary run (contingent on sign-off).
   - 12/10: Target contract signature / production onboarding kickoff.

5) DocuSign: Soojin to send the MAP signature stub (two-page) to Priyanka + legal after 11/20 updates.

Attachments / evidence folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cMAPfolder (I'll post the final v2 spreadsheet there once SOC2 is in).

If there are no objections I'll mark the MAP draft as 'ready for signature' on 11/21 and route via DocuSign.

Thanks —
